title: Negative fractions
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

sections.title: Where the negative sign goes
sections.objective: Write a fraction with its sign in front, and know when two negatives make a positive.
explain: A fraction is a division: {3/5} means 3 ÷ 5. So the sign rules for dividing integers work for fractions too.
One negative, on top or on the bottom, makes the fraction negative: (−3)/5 and 3/(−5) are both −{3/5}. We usually write the sign in front.
Two negatives make a positive: (−6)/(−9) is the same as 6/9, which simplifies to {2/3}.

sections.title: Add and subtract negative fractions
sections.objective: Use a common denominator, then add the tops with the integer rules.
explain: Work just like adding fractions: find a common denominator and rewrite both fractions. The sign comes along with the top.
−{1/2} + {1/3}: the common denominator is 6, so it's −{3/6} + {2/6}. Add the tops with the integer rules: −3 + 2 = −1. The answer is −{1/6}.

sections.title: Multiply and divide negative fractions
sections.objective: Decide the sign first, then multiply or divide the fractions as usual.
explain: Same sign rule as integers: one negative gives a negative answer; two negatives give a positive answer.
−{2/3} × {3/5}: one negative, so the answer is negative. Then {2/3} × {3/5} = {6/15} = {2/5}. The answer is −{2/5}.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.objective: All four operations with negative fractions, mixed together.
explain: Adding or subtracting: common denominator, then the integer rules on the tops. Multiplying or dividing: the sign first, then the fractions. Always simplify.

hints.frac.signed.sign-placement: One negative makes the fraction negative. Two negatives make it positive. Then simplify.
hints.frac.signed.add-sub: Subtracting? Add the opposite. Then use a common denominator and add the tops with the integer rules.
hints.frac.signed.mult-div: Count the negatives: one means a negative answer, two mean positive. Then multiply (or flip and multiply).
hints.frac.signed: Adding or subtracting: common denominator and integer rules. Multiplying or dividing: sign first, then the fractions.

simplifyHint: That's the right amount, but it isn't in simplest form yet. Is there a number that still divides both the top and the bottom?

misconceptionMessages.frac.signed-sign-dropped: One of the numbers is negative, so the fraction is negative. Keep the sign: write it in front.
misconceptionMessages.frac.signed-two-negatives: A negative divided by a negative is positive, so this fraction is positive.
misconceptionMessages.frac.signed-wrong-sign: The size is right, but check the sign: add the tops with the integer rules (keep the sign of the bigger one when the signs are different).
misconceptionMessages.frac.signed-sub-ignored-sign: Watch the second fraction's sign. Subtracting means adding the opposite: subtracting a negative is adding a positive.
misconceptionMessages.frac.signed-mult-sign: The size is right, but check the sign: one negative makes the answer negative; two negatives make it positive.
